title: Advanced Manufacturing: From Research Artifact To Production
summary: Follow manufacturing programs into named facility interventions, repeat output, labor, quality, cost, delivery, demand, and independently validated production outcomes.
current_state_summary: Current Applications, Island Components, and Monaghan Medical now have named before-and-after output panels, with company and MEP attribution kept explicit.
current_state: NSF award 2433348 funds an AI-to-materials institute, while NIST METIS exposes an initial shared-data infrastructure.
NAPMP final awards name packaging recipients, facility functions, substrates, and piloting goals.
NNME Southwest names employers, educators, and workforce organizations intended to coordinate microelectronics training without reporting delivery or worker outcomes.
DOE's Storage STEP prize targets production-process readiness rather than declaring technologies deployment-ready.
MP Materials financing and Talon Nickel award records create named processing trails without proving completed output.
Project Pele's delivered fuel is a physical manufacturing and logistics milestone that still precedes assembly, testing, and operation.
MEP's FY 2021 and FY 2022 client surveys retain sales, savings, investment, and job measures with program attribution.
Manufacturing USA and NIIMBL preserve recurring institute activity, while Census ASM provides an official establishment-level statistical rail.
Three NIST MEP case studies expose compatible before-and-after units within each named line or facility.
Product, labor, quality, cost, demand, follow-up, and attribution differences stop any cross-manufacturer ranking.
Phase 56C adds entity-matched controls, inputs, constraints, later observations, attribution, independent-validation limits, and alternative explanations.
Temporal order is preserved without converting association into causation, ranking, composite scoring, or readiness scoring.
Phase 56D adds later observations and explicit tests of named Phase 56C alternative explanations for the same twelve entities.
Compatibility, attribution, validation status, missing denominators, and series breaks remain visible before any interpretation.
Phase 56E adds a second vertically replicated cohort: Lockheed Martin F-35 Fort Worth final-assembly line, Boeing KC-46A Everett production line, Boeing F-15EX St. Louis production line.
Every retained entity carries a panel, a driver-and-constraint dossier, and an alternative-explanation test under one stable identity.
Phase 56F assigns every entity one highest-value missing record, one strongest compatible current record, a closure state, and an explicit reopening rule.
Across all 24 entities, one bounded record is Closed, sixteen are Partially Closed, and seven remain Open; these are evidence states, not performance measures.
Phase 56G checked 1 exact record rail in this pathway and retained the Phase 56F reopening rules.
The selected exact records remain Open; current adjacent records are preserved as dated checks rather than closures.
Phase 56H checked 3 named records in this pathway against existing coverage IDs and continuation rules.
1 selected evidence state advances from Open to Partially Closed; the remaining denominators stay explicit.
Phase 56I completes 3 first-pass decisions in this pathway while retaining each coverage ID and continuation rule.
No selected closure state changes; genuinely new denominators publish and repeated evidence remains referenced rather than relabeled as a new finding.
Phase 56J adds 1 named continuation decision to this pathway under the ordered evidence-value queue.
Acquisition order describes evidence opportunity and does not rank entities, performance, safety, quality, readiness, or value.
Phase 56K checks 2 exact named records in this pathway and preserves explicit non-closures.
An exact-record check can improve the evidence rail without changing the selected closure state.
Phase 56L adds two certified realized-employment denominators and retains one exact repeat-series non-closure across three manufacturer rails.
Project amount, project completion, current employment, later commitments, and operating output remain distinct evidence types.

evidence_limits: The pathway joins different manufacturing domains to expose conversion stages; it does not imply that one program validates another.
Research awards and shared-data systems do not establish process yield, quality, reliability, throughput, cost, or customer acceptance.
Financial and prize instruments do not prove manufacturing-site readiness, production capacity, bankability, or local benefits.
A workforce consortium does not establish funded training capacity, completed credentials, placement, retention, employer demand, or supplier readiness.
The Southwest link remains a receiving-system question and does not prove that the listed federal records have converted into Arizona supplier or workforce outcomes.
Program respondent mix, follow-up periods, institute coverage, and activity definitions can change between reports.
Nominal dollars, participant counts, project counts, jobs, quality, and productivity cannot be combined without a shared method.
The case studies do not expose a common observation window, product mix, labor input, quality, cost, demand, or follow-up denominator.
A named intervention, control, input, or response does not by itself explain an observed outcome.
Company and operator claims remain attributed until independently validated.
A recommendation status, certification, supplier clause, incident response, monthly cause mix, or complaint count does not create a common performance measure.
Different units, methods, identities, observation windows, and attribution levels remain split.
The second cohort preserves attribution, unit, denominator, method, observation window, reporting breaks, and identity changes.
A vertical entity record does not authorize cross-entity ranking, composite scoring, readiness scoring, or causal inference.
Phase 56F closure states apply to one named missing record per entity and cannot be converted into a ranking, composite, readiness score, or causal claim.
Phase 56G acquisition outcomes measure evidence closure only and cannot be converted into entity performance, a comparison, or a score.
Phase 56H closure and deepening states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56I first-pass and closure states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56J acquisition order and closure states cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56K exact-record decisions cannot be converted into rankings, scores, readiness, quality, safety, value, or causal claims.
Phase 56L realized-outcome records cannot be converted into productivity, ranking, readiness, value, or causal claims.
